claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my 17-year-old, Alex. They live at home with me. I'm just wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 17 years old, there are specific rules that apply. You can normally still qualify for Child Benefit for a child aged 16-19 if they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, studying at school, college, or in approved training)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. They're doing their A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! Since Alex is 17 and in approved education (doing A-levels), that's a good sign.

Now I need to understand a bit more about your living situation and responsibility for Alex:

**Do you live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we both live here in the UK together. Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**Are you currently the person responsible for Alex's day-to-day care and expenses (such as food, clothes, accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I'm responsible for Alex's day-to-day care and all their expenses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

One final question to complete my assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another family member)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 17 years old and currently doing A-levels, which counts as approved education
- You can continue to receive Child Benefit for children aged 16-19 as long as they remain in approved education or training
- You live with Alex in the UK
- You're responsible for Alex's day-to-day care and expenses
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

All the eligibility criteria are met, so you should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex. 

**Important note:** Child Benefit can continue while Alex is in approved education until they turn 20, or until they leave education/training (whichever comes first).

Also, please be aware that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit but may need to pay some or all of it back through your tax return.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
